name: Basilica of San Albino
history: Mesilla's settlers built their first church of mud and logs in 1852 on the plaza, while the town was still in Mexico; the Gadsden Purchase then moved it into the United States. A second church with French features followed, and its first bell was commissioned in 1876. The present church went up on the same site from 1906 to 1908 and became a basilica in 2008.
arch: Fired brick, with a belfry at each front corner and a mission-style parapet between them, on the north side of the town plaza.
features: Leaded stained glass windows show saints, and geometric designs line the nave walls.
It is one of the oldest churches in the region.

look.d: A belfry stands at each corner of the brick front.
The church faces Mesilla's old plaza.

fun: San Albino is Albinus of Angers, a Breton saint born in Vannes, France, in 469.
journal: A parish founded in Mexico that woke up in the U.S. Brick belfries on the plaza.

quiz.q: How did the parish come into the U.S.?
What was the first church built of?

a: Albinus of Angers, a French saint
